purpose: ADR 0032 precondition 7: Cesium-side filtering and aliasing, measured in the shipping renderer.
scratchRootNote: The capture PNGs and the two variant GLB packages live in the gitignored artifacts/ scratch root and are deliberately not committed. Their checksums above keep this record checkable after that tree is removed.

stations.note: Inspection profile: street-level, looking up at the lower facade, well inside the LOD 0 range.
Exploration profile: block seen from across the avenue, several buildings in frame.
Whole ESB shaft in frame: ~160 vertical tile repeats compressed toward the screen-pixel floor.

variants.note: Writer emits wrapS/wrapT only; minification and magnification are whatever the renderer picks.
LINEAR magnification with LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR minification, named in the shipped bytes.

verdict.discardedStation: A first inspection station at 28 m ground distance from the ESB centroid placed the camera INSIDE the ESB footprint and produced an unlit interior; it was discarded as a station-design defect and replaced by inspection-facade at 95 m.
verdict.method: Both sampler variants of the SAME 14-asset V3T package, built from the same plans, loaded through the same object-URL seam, at three identical fixed camera stations. The only difference between the two captures at a station is the sampler.

reading.byteSizeObservation: Capture PNG sizes, reported as an observation and NOT as the metric: inspection-facade 683576 -> 724182 B, exploration-street 675816 -> 719501 B, far-shaft-repeats 453539 -> 427662 B (default -> trilinear). The far station is the only one where trilinear compresses smaller, which is consistent with the default carrying high-frequency energy that is aliasing rather than information. The near stations do not shrink, so mipmapping is not buying its stability by discarding near-field detail. The verdict rests on the visual reading, not on these numbers.
reading.exploration-street: renderer-default shows moire clumping on the upper shaft and a speckled, unstable brick field on the neighbouring masonry buildings. trilinear removes both. Bay rhythm, spandrel bands and floor lines stay fully legible under trilinear.
reading.far-shaft-repeats: DECISIVE. renderer-default breaks the mullion grid into irregular horizontal clumping and speckle across the ESB shaft: the pattern reads as noise banding rather than as coursing, and the apparent floor rhythm is wrong in places. trilinear resolves the same shaft as an even, regular grid with a stable tone and no banding. This is the ~160-vertical-repeat regime ADR 0032 precondition 7 named, and the defect it predicted is present.
reading.inspection-facade: No legibility cost. Under trilinear the ESB curtain grid, the spandrel bands, the floor lines and the window reveals are all read at least as clearly as under renderer-default, and the neighbouring masonry reads as brick rather than as speckle. Nothing that was legible became illegible.

renderer.engine: CesiumJS 1.143.0, EllipsoidTerrainProvider, no imagery, no lighting, requestRenderMode off
renderer.note: This is the shipping renderer. ADR 0032's stills were Blender EEVEE, which is not.
renderer.server: vite preview (production build, VITE_T028_SAMPLER_PROBE=1) on http://localhost:4312

verdict.scope: This closes ADR 0032 precondition 7 for the sampler question only. It does not measure frame time, GPU memory, or mobile behaviour, and it does not admit any package.
verdict.verdict: Leaving minFilter/magFilter unspecified is a real defect in the shipping renderer, not a theoretical one, and it is worst exactly where a citywide textured wave would live: whole towers in frame. LINEAR magnification with LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR minification fixes it at every station tested and costs no measured legibility. Any textured package admitted publicly must name this pair in its shipped bytes.
